name: Castle and Central Kumamoto
tagline: Around the black castle and the covered arcades
description: The centre below Kumamoto Castle, with the Kamitori and Shimotori covered shopping arcades running through it, the tram line, the restaurants and the department stores. The castle's reconstruction after the 2016 earthquakes is visible and ongoing. Everything practical in the city is inside this area.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the castle, the arcades and the trams on foot
pros: The castle and the arcades within a short walk
Trams and buses in every direction
cons: The highest rents in the city
Busy shopping crowds through the day

name: Suizenji
tagline: Around the strolling garden east of the centre
description: The district built around Suizenji Jojuen, a seventeenth-century strolling garden that recreates the fifty-three stations of the Tokaido road in miniature landscape, with a spring-fed pond and a small Mount Fuji. The area around it is quiet and residential with the tram running through.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a quiet district with a garden at the end of the street
pros: Quiet residential streets with the tram through
cons: Ten to fifteen minutes into the centre

name: Kumamoto University Area
tagline: North of the centre, students and cheaper flats
description: The northern district around Kumamoto University, with student apartments, cheap restaurants, bookshops and a young population. Rents here are the lowest close to the centre, and it is the one part of the city where a foreigner has a reasonable chance of finding English speakers outside the tourist sites.
bestFor: Budget stays and anyone with a university connection
pros: The lowest rents near the centre
Best chance of an English-speaking circle

name: Kengun and the Eastern Suburbs
tagline: Along the tram line east, ordinary and good value
description: The residential districts following the tram line east from the centre, with apartment buildings, supermarkets, local restaurants and a settled Japanese population. There is nothing to see, which is exactly why rents are low, and the tram puts the centre fifteen minutes away.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting ordinary Japanese neighbourhood life cheaply
pros: Low rents with a direct tram into the centre
cons: Nothing to see or do locally

name: Mount Aso and the Caldera (45 km east)
tagline: Inside one of the largest calderas on earth
description: The Aso caldera, twenty-five kilometres across with towns, farms and a railway inside it and an active crater at the centre whose access changes with the alert level. The grasslands on the flanks are unlike anywhere else in Japan, and Kurokawa Onsen's wooded hot spring village is nearby.
bestFor: Stays built around the volcano and the onsen rather than the city
pros: The caldera, the crater and the grasslands
Kurokawa Onsen and the region's hot springs
Cool in summer and genuinely spectacular
cons: An hour and a half from the city and a car helps
Crater access closes without notice on alert
